q: By default, a newly created storage account accepts connections from:
opts: Only the VNet it was created in
exp: New accounts allow access from all networks until you restrict them.

q: Which CLI command adds a VNet subnet rule to a storage account firewall?
opts: az storage account network-rule add --account-name st1 --vnet-name VNet1 --subnet SubnetA
az network vnet rule add --storage st1
exp: az storage account network-rule add supports --vnet-name/--subnet and --ip-address.

q: After enabling the firewall with selected networks, an admin can't browse containers in the portal from home. Their data access works from Azure VMs. Why?
opts: The portal requests come from the admin's public IP, which isn't in the IP rules
exp: Portal data operations come from the client's IP, so add the client IP to the firewall rules.

q: Can you add a private IP range (e.g., 10.0.0.0/8) to the storage firewall's IP rules to allow on-premises clients?
opts: No — IP rules accept public IP addresses only; use VNet rules or private endpoints for private ranges
exp: IP network rules only allow public internet IP ranges; private (RFC 1918) ranges aren't allowed.

q: A subnet in a different region from the storage account must be allowed by a VNet rule. What applies?
opts: It's supported: VNet rules can allow subnets in other regions
Must peer the VNet with the storage account
exp: Storage service endpoints support VNets in other regions as well.

q: A storage account needs a private endpoint for both blob and file access. How many private endpoints are required?
opts: Two — one per sub-resource (blob and file)
None; one service endpoint covers both
exp: Each storage service (blob, file, queue, table, web, dfs) needs its own private endpoint.

q: Which private DNS zone name is used for blob private endpoints?
exp: Private endpoints for blob use the privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone.

q: You create a private endpoint and want to block all public internet access to the storage account. Which setting?
exp: Disabling public network access forces traffic through private endpoints only.

q: Which TWO statements about a storage private endpoint are true?
opts: It consumes a private IP from your VNet subnet
It works from on-premises over VPN or ExpressRoute
It requires a service endpoint on the same subnet
It makes the account publicly readable
exp: Private endpoints get a VNet IP and are reachable from connected networks. They don't require a service endpoint.

q: What does 'Secure transfer required' do on a storage account?
opts: Rejects requests made over HTTP (and SMB without encryption)
exp: Secure transfer enforces HTTPS for REST calls and encrypted SMB.

q: Security policy says clients must use TLS 1.2 or later. Which storage setting?
exp: Set the minimum TLS version on the account to reject older TLS.

q: Which SAS type can grant access to multiple services (blob, file, queue, table) in a single token?
exp: An account SAS can cover multiple services and service-level operations.

q: In a SAS URL, which parameter holds the expiry time?
exp: se = signed expiry; sp = permissions; sv = version; sig = signature.

q: In a SAS URL, 'sp=rl' means:
exp: sp lists permissions: r = read, l = list, w = write, d = delete, and so on.

q: Security requires blocking all SAS signed with account keys while still allowing Entra-based access. What do you configure?
opts: Disable 'Allow storage account key access' (shared key authorization)
exp: Disabling shared key authorization blocks account keys, account SAS, and service SAS. User delegation SAS (Entra) still works.

q: What is the maximum validity of a user delegation SAS?
opts: 7 days (limited by the user delegation key)
exp: The user delegation key, and therefore the SAS, can be valid for at most 7 days.

q: Which CLI command generates a SAS for a single blob?
exp: az storage blob generate-sas creates a blob-level SAS token.

q: A SAS token works in testing, then fails for a partner a week later with 403 errors. Which is the most likely cause?
opts: The SAS expired (se passed) or the signing key was rotated
exp: SAS failures usually come from expiry, key rotation, IP/protocol restrictions, or firewall rules.

q: Which levels can have a stored access policy?
exp: Stored access policies are defined on containers, shares, queues, and tables.

q: A SAS references stored access policy 'p1'. You delete p1 and create a new policy with the same name 'p1'. What happens to the old SAS?
opts: It becomes valid again under the new p1's settings
exp: SAS tokens reference the policy by name. Recreating the same name re-associates them, so use new names when revoking.

q: How long can it take for a change to a stored access policy to take effect?
exp: Changes to stored access policies can take up to 30 seconds to apply.

q: Order the steps to rotate storage account keys with no downtime:
items: Update applications back to key1 (new value)
exp: Switch apps to key2 → regenerate key1 → switch apps to the new key1 → regenerate key2.

q: Which CLI command regenerates the primary storage key?
opts: az storage account keys renew --account-name st1 --key primary
exp: az storage account keys renew with --key primary or secondary.

q: Which role lets a user list storage account access keys?
opts: Storage Account Key Operator Service Role (or Contributor/Owner)
exp: Listing keys requires Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action, which roles like Storage Account Key Operator Service Role and Contributor include.

q: What does a key expiration policy on a storage account do?
opts: Flags keys that are older than the set interval (in Azure Policy/Advisor) so you know to rotate them
exp: A key expiration policy sets a rotation reminder interval; it doesn't rotate keys automatically.

q: An app must upload and delete blobs using its managed identity. Least-privilege role?
exp: Blob Data Contributor allows read, write, and delete on blob data. Owner also manages POSIX ACLs.

q: A user must manage POSIX ACLs on a Data Lake Storage Gen2 account. Which role?
exp: Only Storage Blob Data Owner can set ownership and manage POSIX access control.

q: An app must read messages from an Azure Storage queue using Entra ID. Which role?
opts: Storage Queue Data Message Processor (or Queue Data Reader)
Storage File Data SMB Share Reader
exp: Queue data roles grant access to queue messages.

q: What's the narrowest scope at which you can assign Storage Blob Data Reader?
exp: Blob data roles can be assigned down to the container scope (not individual blobs). Use ABAC conditions for finer control.

q: Which portal setting makes the portal use Entra ID instead of access keys when browsing blob data?
opts: Default to Microsoft Entra authorization in the Azure portal
exp: Enabling 'Default to Microsoft Entra authorization' makes the portal use Entra ID for data access.

q: Which share-level role lets users read, write, and delete files over SMB, but not change NTFS permissions?
opts: Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor
Storage File Data SMB Share Reader
Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor
exp: Contributor = read/write/delete; Elevated Contributor can also modify NTFS ACLs; Reader = read only.

q: Administrators must change NTFS permissions on folders in an Azure file share. Which share-level role do they need?
opts: Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor
Storage File Data SMB Share Reader
exp: Elevated Contributor includes modifying Windows ACLs.

q: All authenticated identities should get the same share-level permission without individual assignments. What do you use?
exp: A default share-level permission applies to all authenticated users when no specific role is assigned.

q: To enable on-premises AD DS authentication for Azure Files, the storage account must be:
opts: Joined/registered to the AD DS domain as a computer or service logon account (for example, with the AzFilesHybrid module)
exp: The storage account is represented in AD DS as an identity, usually set up with AzFilesHybrid's Join-AzStorageAccount.

q: Which identities must users have for AD DS authentication to Azure Files to work?
opts: Hybrid identities synced to Entra ID via Entra Connect
exp: AD DS auth requires users synced to Entra ID so share-level RBAC can be assigned.

q: Answer Yes or No about Azure Files access:
stmts: The storage account key can still mount a share even when identity-based auth is enabled
NTFS permissions alone are enough without any share-level permission
Azure Files supports identity-based auth over SMB
SAS tokens can be used to mount SMB shares
exp: The key works like a superuser; share-level permission is needed; SMB identity auth is supported; SAS works for REST access, not SMB mounts.

q: Security wants to make sure no container in an account can ever be set to public. Which account setting?
exp: Disabling anonymous access at the account level overrides container settings.

q: With the 'Container' anonymous access level, anonymous users can:
opts: Read blobs and list the blobs in the container
exp: Container level allows anonymous read of blobs and listing. Writes are never anonymous.

ctx: Storage account st1 has the firewall set to selected networks with SubnetA allowed. A user on VM1 in SubnetB uses a valid SAS.
q: Will the request succeed?
opts: Yes, a valid SAS always works
No, the firewall still blocks traffic from networks that aren't allowed
exp: Network rules are evaluated in addition to authorization, so a valid SAS can't bypass the firewall.

q: Which authorization method does Microsoft recommend for blob access from Azure-hosted apps?
opts: Microsoft Entra ID with managed identities
exp: Entra ID with managed identity avoids secrets and supports least privilege.

q: Which TWO methods let you revoke access that was granted via SAS?
opts: Delete or modify the stored access policy the SAS references
Regenerate the account key that signed the SAS
exp: Revoke policy-based SAS through the policy; ad-hoc SAS through key rotation. (User delegation SAS can also be revoked by revoking the delegation keys.)

q: How do you invalidate all user delegation SAS tokens immediately?
opts: Revoke all user delegation keys for the account
exp: Revoking user delegation keys (az storage account revoke-delegation-keys) invalidates all user delegation SAS.

q: Which statement about CORS on a storage account is correct?
opts: CORS rules let browser apps from specific origins call storage endpoints
exp: CORS rules allow cross-origin browser requests from permitted origins.

q: Order the steps so that only VNet1/SubnetA can reach storage account st1:
items: Add a VNet rule for VNet1/SubnetA on st1
Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on SubnetA
Set st1 public network access to 'Enabled from selected networks'
Test access from a VM in SubnetA
exp: Enable the service endpoint → switch to selected networks → add the VNet rule → test.

q: Which feature allows specific Azure resource instances (for example, one Synapse workspace) through the storage firewall?
exp: Resource instance rules grant access to specific resource instances based on their managed identity.

q: Different containers in one storage account must be encrypted with different customer-managed keys. Which feature?
exp: Encryption scopes let you manage encryption at the container or blob level with different keys.

q: Which identity does a storage account use to access the customer-managed key in Key Vault?
opts: A managed identity (system- or user-assigned) with key permissions
exp: The storage account authenticates to Key Vault with a managed identity that has the needed key permissions.

q: What happens to blob access if the customer-managed key is disabled in Key Vault?
opts: Data operations fail with 403 until the key is re-enabled
The account switches to Microsoft-managed keys
exp: Without the key, the service can't decrypt data, so access fails until the key is restored.

q: With customer-managed keys, which option lets Azure Storage automatically use the newest key version after rotation?
opts: Specify the key URI without a version (automatic key version updates)
exp: Omitting the version enables automatic updates to the latest key version.

ctx: st1: firewall = selected networks (SubnetA, office IP 203.0.113.10), shared key access disabled, public anonymous access disabled.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A VM in SubnetA with a managed identity holding Storage Blob Data Reader can read blobs
A user at the office using an account SAS can read blobs
An anonymous user on the internet can read a blob by URL
A user at the office with Storage Blob Data Reader can read blobs in the portal (Entra auth)
exp: Entra auth from allowed networks works; account SAS needs shared key auth, which is disabled; anonymous access is disabled; the office IP is allowed and Entra auth works.
